verified_facts_for_writer.technical_debt_cost: Industry estimates (smartShift): maintaining/testing/upgrading unused custom code costs ~USD 0.25-0.63 per line of code per year; an average SAP ECC system carries ~22,000 custom objects and ~2.7M lines of custom code; ~40-60% of custom code is technically unused. VERIFY/attribute as smartShift industry estimate (not SAP official); label as estimate.
verified_facts_for_writer.tco_reduction: Vendor/analyst estimates put clean-core TCO reduction at ~40-55% within three years (SAVIC/ITP/scmchamps); some cite ~30-40% lower annual maintenance. These are vendor estimates - the writer MUST frame as ranges/estimates, attribute the source, and NOT present as guaranteed. Prefer SAP-official or analyst (Gartner/IDC/Forrester) numbers where available.
verified_facts_for_writer.extensibility_levels_A_D: SAP formalized a four-level model (A-D) in Aug 2025. Level A: released/public stable APIs only (ABAP Cloud on-stack or side-by-side on BTP), backed by stability contracts, fully upgrade-safe - target for new development. Level B: classic ABAP using only officially provided APIs/frameworks (legacy APIs, BAdIs, user exits) - allowed when Level A insufficient; needs governance. Level C: uses SAP internal/unclassified objects - not cloud-ready, meaningful upgrade risk, belongs on remediation roadmap (SAP plans a changelog to flag object changes early). Level D: explicitly non-recommended (core modifications, write access to SAP tables, implicit enhancements) - highest risk, eliminate. Source: SAP Community 'ABAP Extensibility Guide - Clean Core (Aug 2025 Update)' + SAP News 2025/08 + avotechs summary.
verified_facts_for_writer.release_maintenance_cadence: S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition ships semi-annual releases (Feb/Aug). From the 2023 release SAP moved to a two-year release cycle with 7 years mainstream maintenance (up from 5); Continuous Feature Delivery adds innovations between majors. This is WHY upgrade-safe extensions matter - upgrades are now frequent/continuous. VERIFY current cadence wording against SAP help/learning before printing.
verified_facts_for_writer.fit_to_standard: Fit-to-standard = shift from 'change the software to fit our process' to 'adapt our process to the software's best practice' ('why-not-standard' mindset). SAP guidance: every requirement passes a two-question test (can standard meet it? if not, can a Level A/B extension?). Hardest barriers are organizational/cultural (delivery pressure, under-resourced governance, resistance to standard, habit of custom code), not technical. Sources: SAP Learning 'Managing Clean Core' course; IgniteSAP; sap-press blog.
verified_facts_for_writer.coe: SAP Center of Excellence (CoE) = internal team owning SAP lifecycle: process design, enhancements, project delivery, training, governance. Common 4-part structure: leadership/steering, core team (day-to-day + small enhancements), extended team (SME by area), project teams (temporary). Build options: in-house / outsourced / hybrid. Governance provides strategic direction + accountability. Sources: Surety Systems, Eursap, SAPinsider, SAP Customer COE guides.
verified_facts_for_writer.regulated_industry: In regulated industries (pharma/life sciences GxP, banking, food) some customization is mandatory for compliance (21 CFR Part 11, EU GMP Annex 11, audit trails, validation). Clean core here means: keep mandatory compliance extensions clean-core-compliant (Level A/B, decoupled) so validation/re-qualification effort is minimised on each upgrade. Sources: SNP Group, IntuitionLabs, Assima, SAP Community GxP public-cloud post. Indonesian context: Coretax/Core Tax Administration System (DJP, live Jan 2025) and OJK requirements are localization/compliance drivers; ERP can integrate to Coretax via official API. VERIFY OJK-specific claims before printing (search found no clean-core-specific OJK source).
verified_facts_for_writer.pragmatic_myth: Clean core is NOT a ban on customization - it is responsible/controlled extensibility placed OUTSIDE the core. 'There are 50 shades of clean core' (TechTarget). Deloitte/community sources push a pragmatic reading. Useful for the honest/counter-conventional H2s.
verified_facts_for_writer.ecc_dates: SAP ECC (EHP 6-8) mainstream maintenance ends 31 Dec 2027; extended maintenance to end of 2030 for a fee (~+2% / ~9% cited variously - VERIFY exact surcharge); select RISE/private-cloud customers can reach 2033 with conditions. Compatibility Packs final transition extended to 31 May 2026. Migrations take ~18-36 months. VERIFY all dates/surcharges against the live SAP maintenance-strategy page + Forrester before printing - they have shifted historically. Sources: SAP support maintenance-strategy page; SEIDOR; SAVIC; Forrester (cited in prior cluster articles -03/-05).
